title: Commercial Promissory Note
text: “So, thanks to Keel and the others, I’ve managed to get my hands on some alchemy recipes and other stuff. I still have to make some things from scratch, but alchemy is actually pretty fun.”
My father gave me an update on how things were going, as if it were just casual small talk.
“So, Father. I’d forgotten to ask—could you tell me the name of the inn where you stayed on the first day of your adventure?”
“Hm? Why?”
My father asked me, looking a little annoyed.
“Just in case, you know.”
“Ah, I see.”

Realizing my intention, Father nodded. That’s right—if I just know which inn Father is staying at, it’ll be useful information in case we end up in a loop. I haven’t figured out exactly how to use it yet, but it’ll definitely come in handy.
“Well, since we have a little time before our appointment, why don’t we swing by?”
“That sounds good. So, Sakura-chan. On Kou’s behalf, I’d like to ask you to take on the role of protecting my father from now on.”
“Gua!”
Sakura-chan walked over to my father and started playfully nuzzling him.
“Ahaha, that tickles, Sakura-chan.”
“Guaaa…”
Sakura-chan looked really happy to be reunited with my father. With that cheerful atmosphere still in the air, we headed over, and my father told us the name of the inn.
“The room at this inn… oh yeah, right there.”
I made a mental note of the room my Father pointed to. If we ever come back here, having this information will make a huge difference.
“You’re the Shield Hero, aren’t you?”
“I guess so…”
On our way to the meeting spot, a Demi-Human called out to my Father.
“What? Do you want something from me?”
“I have a humble request… Would you be willing to visit our country, Shieldfreeden?”

Oh? This is the second time my Father has been approached. I remember seeing some suspicious-looking people myself, but so it turns out Shieldfreeden had also sent a recruitment offer. As I watched silently, my Father groaned thoughtfully.
“I’m sorry, but I’ll have to decline.”

I’m sharing my knowledge of the future with my Father. There should be Takt and his entourage—those Aotatsu women—in Shieldfreeden. Going there would be like a moth flying into a flame. There’s no need to walk right into a trap like that.
“Please don’t say that—couldn’t you just come? We’ve made special arrangements to treat you with the utmost respect should you join us.”
“Hmm…”
My father turns his gaze toward me.
“I’m still turning you down. I’ve got things I need to take care of.”
“Please, just this once! Could you please come? It would be for the good of the Demi-Human accompanying you, too.”
“Even if you say that… I mean, you’re being pretty persistent…”
Furrowing his brow, my father shows his displeasure. I suspect that back when he was in his wild days, he might have hurled some insults here?
“Yeah, I’m going to do things my way, so don’t follow me. I declare this as the Shield Hero.”
“Tsk! Don’t say I didn’t warn you!”

The Demi-Human walked away, clicking his tongue in some sort of annoyance. Just as you’d expect from people from a country under Takt’s control. Once everything is settled, I, Motoyasu, will personally deal with them. Along with Takt and his cronies, mind you.
“That was pretty rude… The people from Siltvelt were more polite, weren’t they? Well, they were just as persistent, though.”
“Was that so?”
“Yeah. When I told them I couldn’t go to your country because I had things to do, they wouldn’t let it go. It was a real hassle to negotiate with them.”
“So we’re going to negotiate again, right?”
“Yeah. I told them I’d talk to them again tomorrow since I thought it’d be better if Motoyasu-kun was there, and they backed off.”
Otherwise, he’d have played that trump card—refusing as the Shield Hero. Just as I’d expect from my Father; as long as things aren’t getting heated, he won’t turn them down lightly.
“Boo-boo-boo-hee?”
“Oh, sorry. Did you want to go, Keel?”
“Boo…”

My Father and Keel are talking, but I can’t make heads or tails of it. However, Keel seems to be shaking his head. Judging by the context of the conversation, it’s probably something along the lines of not having to go to Shieldfreeden.
“Well then, let’s go talk to the envoy from Siltvelt.”
Guided by my Father, we headed off to speak with the envoy from Siltvelt.

A tavern tucked away in a back alley of the castle town… It seems to be frequented by many Demi-Human adventurers. So there are places like this in Melromarc, too. I didn’t know that. It didn’t look like it was doing much business, but it seemed my father-in-law had arranged to meet the envoy here. Yuki-chan and the others waited outside the tavern to keep watch.
“Shield Hero, have you had a chance to think about yesterday’s matter?”
“Well, about that…”
My father-in-law gestured toward me, signaling the envoy from Siltvelt to look my way.
“First, let’s start with introductions. This is Motoyasu Kitamura. He was summoned as the Spear Hero.”
“I am Motoyasu Kitamura, The Love Hunter.”
“He’s a bit eccentric, but he’s someone you can really count on.”
I am a hunter who lives for love. That will never change, for all eternity. For some reason, my Father says I’m eccentric—but is there really something odd about me?
“We’ve heard reports from various sources. Thank you so much for standing up for the Shield Hero.”
“I was just doing what anyone should do.”

That’s right… The sin I committed—not knowing the truth—is something that can never be forgiven, no matter how many times I loop. But I can no longer stand by and watch as my Father is about to be lured into a trap right before my eyes. No matter how many times I loop, I will always act to protect my Father.
“Anyway, getting back to the main point—I still can’t go to Siltvelt.”
“W-why is that?”
“It’s not that I’m the scourge of this country, but I lament this nation’s exclusion of Demi-Humans, and I want to do something about it. So I have no intention of going to your country on a whim.”

The envoy from Siltvelt furrowed his brow in a troubled manner. Well, their job is to escort my Father to Siltvelt, after all. Apparently, the fact that they aren’t very strong is because this was an emergency and they just happened to be nearby.
“So what do you plan to do in this country?”
“Just being the Shield Hero makes people wary of me, so I’m thinking of hiding my identity for a while and maybe working as a traveling merchant.”
“I see… But do you have a commercial pass?”
“A commercial pass?”

My Father turns his gaze toward me. Without hesitation, I shook my head. I have no idea. As far as I know, my Father made his fortune and earned his reputation through peddling. Perhaps he acquired a commercial pass somewhere along the way?
“Peddlers without a commercial pass have to pay hefty fees in every town.”
“Is that so?”

It seems a flaw in our plan has been exposed. Since my Father was a traveling merchant in the first world, I thought we could pull this off without any problems. However, it looks like we’ll end up losing money on every trade we make.

“I understand your reasoning, Shield Hero. Well then, as a gesture of cooperation from Siltvelt, I’ll try to negotiate with a noble here who has friendly ties with your country to have them issue you a commercial pass.”
The envoys from Siltvelt seem to be responding with goodwill to us, who are left speechless.
“Ah, thank you… but as the Shield Hero, it doesn’t look like I’ll be able to visit your country just yet…”

“We have certainly received the Shield Hero’s will. Melromarc’s actions since the incident during this wave have been utterly intolerable. If the Shield Hero says He will bestow both blessings and divine punishment for this, our country will surely agree.”
“I’m glad you understand.”

However… it turns out that peddling goods requires quite a bit of hassle. I had no idea. My future Father is the type to let his actions speak for themselves. Well, my future Father never bothered to tell me anything I didn’t need to know, did he? HAHAHA!
“Also… well, if you’ll keep it a secret that the Shield Hero has come to Siltvelt… I might just go there for a little while.”
“What!?”
“Um…”
My father explained my portal skill to the envoy from Siltvelt.
“Lately, I’ve been leveling up over in Siltvelt. Eventually, my father plans to go there in secret as well.”
“Well, it might just be a simple request for help with leveling up and helping my party members go through the Class Up process… you know?”
“Understood. If you’re coming discreetly, we have no reason to refuse. I’ll relay this to our country’s leadership.”
“Thanks in advance.”
“Then, I’ll go ahead and arrange things. I should be able to provide you with a commercial pass within a few days.”
And just like that, I was able to wrap up my conversation with the envoy from Siltvelt.
